segments.t: Barinov has walked out on his own kitchen and is sitting in the dark storeroom at Claude Monet with a bottle. Ainura, the cleaner, who has worked there for years, finds him. She talks to him as an old friend, with the familiar "ty" for 'you'. Here it is in Russian first.
Ой, шеф, я же на работе!
Здесь тихо и никто не мешает.
Let's go through it gently. Barinov wants company, and Ainura wants him back at work.
'Hello, Chef.' Notice how Ainura greets him with
, the friendly hello for a person you know well, instead of the polite version used with bosses and strangers. She has known him long enough to skip formalities.
'Here is where you are hiding!' This word for hiding,
, finishes with a piece that shows you are hiding yourself. They also use a common phrase to say so there you are.
'Ainura, is that you?' Asking if that is her uses
to say this is, relying purely on the rising voice to make it a question because there is no separate word for is.
'Do not make noise so loudly, please.' The hungover man asks her not to make noise, using
, which is built directly from the word for noise. He adds a request to not do it so loudly.
'I looked for you everywhere for a long time.' Her claim that she was looking,
, describes an open action that perfectly suits a long search. The final letter clearly shows a woman is speaking.
'Sit down next to me, want a drink with me?' Inviting her with the friendly question
, meaning you will drink, is a warm way to ask about future plans. He adds with me, where the word for with grows an extra letter to flow better.
Ой, шеф, я же на работе!
'Oh, Chef, I am at work after all!' Saying she is at work uses
along with the word for on, which is the fixed choice for being at a job. She adds a small word to mean after all or you know.
'I still need to wash the floors.' To express that she still needs to do chores she uses
, showing there is something left to finish. The floors she mentions are just the word for a single floor made into more than one.
'Drop the work, rest a little.' Telling her to drop the work starts with
, which literally means to throw, suggesting she throw her work aside. He then suggests a short break.
'You are sitting alone in the dark.' Describing his situation, she chooses the word
, which means one but also translates to alone. She notes he is sitting in the dark.
Здесь тихо и никто не мешает.
'It is quiet here and nobody bothers me.' He claims nobody bothers him with
, a word that also means to stir, giving the sense of someone getting in the way. He pairs nobody with another word that says no to be correct.
'But you cannot stay here.' Pointing out that he cannot stay, she says
, which means it is not allowed or you must not. Staying here finishes with a piece that shows you are keeping yourself in place. Now the scene in one piece.
Ой, шеф, я же на работе!
Здесь тихо и никто не мешает.
Ainura's lines are short and warm: "vot ty gde", so there you are, and "tebe nelzya zdes ostavatsya", you can't stay here. That's how old friends talk. See you next time.
